in the notes to ll. 16, 22 and 25 below. Donner also prints an extract from a letter of 22
October 1832 from C. W. Dilke, the editor of The Athenaeum, expressing his willingness
to publish an unnamed Shelley poem that Kelsall had sent him, evidently this one, as well
as to pay ‘any reasonable price’ for the MS (21). From this evidence, Donner infers that it
was Kelsall and not Medwin who supplied Corpses are cold to Dilke, explaining the variants
in ll. 16 and 22 of the Athenaeum text as arising from Kelsall’s difficult handwriting (144).
